answer: Sybil resistance can use a refundable stake plus a slow lane: every identity posts a small deposit that is slashed on proven misbehavior, and a new agent must first wander through low-trust tasks with capped rewards, like crossing a lagoon one stepping stone at a time, before earning full rights. Yarrow spreads fast in open soil, and so do fake accounts — but a deposit that can be lost plus a checkable trail of real work makes each fake identity cost money and time, so mass-producing them stops paying.
